== Course of events ==

Alice's mention of Dinah, her cat at home, has sent the gathered birds into flight, each fearing to be hunted by so fearsome a creature. Left alone in the quiet that follows, Alice grieves over the carelessness of her own words, understanding now the alarm she has caused. She settles into a patient, sorrowful waiting, her heart held by a single hope—that the Mouse, with whom she had been conversing, might return to her side. In that solitude, she waits sadly, turning over in her mind both her affection for Dinah and her longing for the Mouse's forgiveness or renewed companionship.
